text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayerInMajorTennis(x) ::: x is among the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
IgaSwiathek(x) ::: x is Iga Świątek.
RolandGorros2022(x) ::: x is a female tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
MalePlayerAtRG22(x) ::: x is a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
RafaelNadal(x) ::: x is Rafael Nadal.
CocoGauff(x) ::: x is Coco Gauff.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayerInMajorTennis(x)) ::: If a player is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are among the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostTo(x, IgaSwiathek) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
∀x (RolandGorros2022(x) → LostTo(x, IgaSwiathek)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
(RolandGorros2022(x) ∨ MalePlayerAtRG22(x)) ::: Either female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 or male tennis players at Roland Garros 2022.
∀x (MalePlayerAtRG22(x) → LostTo(x, RafaelNadal)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
∃x ((RankedHighly(x) ∨ LostTo(x, RafaelNadal)) → ¬(MalePlayerAtRG22(x))) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then she is not a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
LostTo(CocoGauff, RafaelNadal)
